The top 100 coins

Source: vignettes/market.Rmd
market.Rmd

The Top 100 and Treemap tabs of the golemcrypto app show the coins with the largest market cap. In R, get_listings() downloads them, plot_treemap() draws the treemap and listings_table() shows the table.

Set up an API key

The listings come from the CoinMarketCap API, which needs a free API key. The price charts of Price charts in R and Volatility, drawdowns and seasonality do not need one.

  1. Sign up at coinmarketcap.com/api and copy your API key.
  2. Open your .Renviron file with usethis::edit_r_environ().
  3. Add this line with your own key, save the file and restart R:
COINMARKETCAP_APIKEY=your-api-key

To use a key for the current R session only, set it with Sys.setenv():

Sys.setenv(COINMARKETCAP_APIKEY = "your-api-key")

Keep the key out of your scripts and out of Git: anyone who has it can use your API credits.

Download the listings 

library(golemcrypto)
listings <- get_listings()
listings$time
#> [1] "2026-11-22 21:15:14 EET"
head(listings$data$name_symbol, 10)
#>  [1] "Bitcoin (BTC)"      "Ethereum (ETH)"     "Tether USDt (USDT)" "BNB (BNB)"          "USDC (USDC)"        "XRP (XRP)"          "Solana (SOL)"       "TRON (TRX)"         "Hyperliquid (HYPE)"
#> [10] "Zcash (ZEC)"
names(listings$data)
#>  [1] "name_symbol"                  "USD_price"                    "USD_volume_24h"               "USD_volume_change_24h"        "USD_percent_change_24h"       "USD_percent_change_7d"       
#>  [7] "USD_percent_change_30d"       "USD_percent_change_60d"       "USD_percent_change_90d"       "USD_market_cap"               "USD_market_cap_dominance"     "USD_fully_diluted_market_cap"
#> [13] "USD_last_updated"

listings$data has a row per coin, sorted by market cap, with the price, the volume, the price changes from 24 hours to 90 days, the market cap and the dominance, all in US dollars. listings$time is when it was downloaded.

Each download uses one credit of your key. get_listings() downloads the listings at most once every 10 minutes, and in between it returns the last download. When a download fails, listings$problem says why, for example when the key has used up its credits.

Treemap

plot_treemap() draws a box per coin, sized by its market cap and colored from red to green by its price change over 24 hours:

plot_treemap(listings$data)

Table

listings_table() shows the listings as a sortable table. Losses are shaded red and gains green, more strongly the larger the change:

listings_table(listings$data)

Like the other charts, plot_treemap() takes mode = "dark" for a dark page, and htmlwidgets::saveWidget() saves the treemap or the table as a web page.
